relations.subject: tool:cbbackupmgr
relations.evidence: Bucket level data may be backed up/restored using the `data_backup` (Data Backup & Restore) role.

relations.subject: tool:cbbackupmgr
relations.evidence: Backing up/restoring cluster level data requires additional RBAC roles, each of which is highlighted below: Analytics Synonyms `analytics_admin` (Analytics Admin)

notable_absence.finding: 'The `data_backup` role does not have access to cluster level data such as: * Analytics Synonyms * Eventing Metadata * FTS Aliases' is a clean doesNotSupport-shaped statement (a bounded non-support boundary, already a promoted predicate), but its object is a bulleted list of three named data categories rather than a single concept, and none of Analytics Synonyms / Eventing Metadata / FTS Aliases yet has its own confident concept id in this registry (eventing:eventing-storage is the metadata KEYSPACE, not 'Eventing Metadata' as a backed-up artifact - a related but not identical thing). Left unminted rather than force a fit; flagged so a reconciler with a clearer view of the eventing/analytics/fts namespaces can split this into three well-typed triples.

cross_component_finding: This page's RBAC section names the exact same three cluster-level roles (Analytics Admin, Eventing Full Admin, Search Admin) as are required for the equivalent flags on cbbackupmgr-config.md's --disable-cluster-analytics/--disable-eventing/--disable-ft-alias options, giving independent, cross-page confirmation that cbbackupmgr's cluster-level-metadata categories (Analytics Synonyms, Eventing Metadata, FTS Aliases) form one consistent triad across the whole tool, not just this page's testing utility.
cross_product_finding: None found on this page specific to Capella; generate is explicitly a testing-only subcommand with no restore/backup semantics of its own, so it does not bear on the module's no-Capella-twin framing.
